_about: Why each class and relation exists, the question it answers, and who confirmed it.

Objective.alternatives: SuccessCriterion only: rejected, a criterion cannot say what it is for beyond the promise. Objective as text on each criterion: rejected, repeats and cannot group. StrategicTheme class: rejected, only if themes are managed outside the product.
Objective.question: What are we trying to achieve this period, and are we on track? Where does this product sit in the strategy? (G1, G2; Gate 3 review)
Objective.why: An objective is dated, owned and superseded, and criteria hang off it; strategic alignment is an objective supporting a higher one, which no attribute can express.

Feature.alternatives: Epic and Story: rejected, Story is a delivery unit and ties the product model to one method. Capability: same thing, the user kept the name Feature.
Feature.question: What is the product made of? (D4)
Feature.why: Builders decompose the product into user-visible capabilities, each traced to a requirement; nesting through part_of lets epics and sub-features share one class.

UserJourney.alternatives: Journey as text on Persona: rejected, nothing could reference it.
UserJourney.question: How does a user get value, step by step? (D1)
UserJourney.why: Design and tests must follow the same path; the journey is the path, owned by a persona and delivering a value proposition.

JourneyStep.alternatives: Steps as an ordered list attribute: rejected, nothing can point at a step. Adding Screen: deferred to the design-vocabulary interview.
JourneyStep.question: How does a user get value, step by step? (D1)
JourneyStep.why: A step has identity of its own: a design decision, a requirement or a test points at one step, which a list attribute on the journey cannot support.

Term.alternatives: Lexicon only: rejected, no citable definition. Term with a Domain grouping class: rejected, only if one word means two things in two contexts of one product.
Term.question: What does this word mean here, who said so, and has the meaning changed? (G7; Gate 3 review)
Term.why: A definition needs a citation and a date so a changed meaning is superseded, which the search lexicon cannot hold; the lexicon is generated from terms instead.

part_of.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
part_of.question: What does this belong to?
part_of.why: Containment is needed by features, steps and anything an extension structures; one relation serves them all. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

realises.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
realises.question: Which requirement does this satisfy?
realises.why: Connects the capability to the need, so an unrealised requirement is visible. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.

pursues.question: Which objectives does the product work towards?
pursues.why: The product-level alignment edge, usually derived from the promises it offers.

supports.question: What strategy does this product serve? (G2)
supports.why: Alignment is recorded as one objective supporting another, so no theme or strategy class is needed.

defines.alternatives: A closed list of classes per side: rejected, two ontologies extending the same base could not both add to it.
defines.question: What does this word name?
defines.why: Binds a term to the entity it names, so a changed meaning is superseded, not argued. One relation with an open side rather than a closed list of classes, so independent ontologies that extend this one compose without redeclaring it; the engine refuses two siblings widening the same relation.
